scope: Replace the asymptotic FMT sigma*y evaluation by an explicit one-sided upper bound, including the exact prime-interval endpoints and the locally excluded prime B0. This contract does not close the prime-distribution package or compute X_cert.

source_definitions.sigma: product over primes a<p<=z, p!=B0 of (1-1/p)
source_definitions.endpoint_semantics: P(z)/P(a) exactly matches the strict lower and inclusive upper prime endpoints

cases: B0=1 or B0 outside (a,z]: no correction
B0 prime in (a,z]: divide P(z)/P(a) by (1-1/B0)

cutoff.interpretation: A sufficient inherited cutoff for this sublemma, not the smallest possible cutoff and not X_cert.

proved_statement: For every real x>=2*exp(36^5), and for either B0=1 or a prime B0, sigma*y<(1001000/998001)*80*c*x*log_2(x)<(26/25)*80*c*x*log_2(x).

literature_assessment.primary_choice: Use the original Rosser-Schoenfeld Theorem 7 rather than reproving an explicit Mertens product theorem.
literature_assessment.dusart_role: Independent later cross-check with a sufficient 0.2/log(t)^2 upper error.
literature_assessment.axler_caution: The published PDF's displayed Proposition 9 upper formula was not adopted because, as printed, it lacks the asymptotic leading term needed for a valid upper bound. This does not affect the directly cited Rosser-Schoenfeld theorem.
literature_assessment.novelty_caution: The project proves only the missing application bridge and makes no worldwide novelty claim.

next_gate.description: Build the full quantitative Proposition 9.2 identity-form composition: one common exceptional B, Bordignon remainder, exact half-open recentering, psi-to-pi conversion, represented-prime density, and a common cutoff.
